title: The Erdős similarity conjecture for geometric progressions
description: For every q in (0, 1), a compact subset of [0, 1] of measure as close to 1 as we like contains no affine copy x + s{q^n : n ≥ 1}, s ≠ 0, so geometric progressions are not measure universal. Random tables on nested dyadic grids route every point through a finite ordered tree; the first default choice on the route of a center offers many independent chances to hit a copy, windows of indices with gaps keep earlier decisions unchanged, and finitely many dilations represent all of them. The course is an exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) of the geometric-progression case of the Erdős similarity conjecture.

units.title: Measure-universal sets and periodic hitting sets
Dyadic grids and windows on a tree

prerequisites: core course Measure and Integration (Fremlin, Measure Theory, Volumes 1 and 2): countable additivity and continuity of measures (112C), translation invariance of Lebesgue measure (134A), outer regularity of Lebesgue outer measure (134F(a)), linear changes of variables (263A)
